newsitem.title: FINLAND: REUTERS AND STT SAY TO CO-PRODUCE NEWS IN FINNISH.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS AND STT SAY TO CO-PRODUCE NEWS IN FINNISH.

text.p: International news and information company Reuters and the Finnish news agency STT said on Monday they will start co-producing economic news in Finnish for media and financial market customers.

The service, to be delivered hourly during the business day, will be made up of mainly short news stories about the latest business and financial developments, Reuters and STT said in a joint statement.
"The package will be based on material from both STT and Reuters," the agencies said. The new service would be launched at the end of summer.
The emphasis will be on Finnish business news produced by Reuters Finnish journalists who currently write for the Finnish financial markets in English and by STT's staff, they said.

"We are delighted to be cooperating with STT on producing news in Finnish. This shows that we are very committed to being an important part of the financial media scene in Finland," Reuters manager in Finland Hans-Petter Bjornestad said.
STT managing director Kari Vaisanen said STT's goal was to "expand our economic news service and make it better to our customers through cooperation with Reuters."
Their cooperation announcement came after a flurry of recent restructuring moves in the world of Finnish financial media.

Privately-controlled Sanoma Oy, publisher of Finland's biggest daily newspaper Helsingin Sanomat, has said it will start publishing a business daily to rival media group Aamulehti-yhtyma Oy's Kauppalehti paper.
Talentum Oy , publisher of leading business weekly Talouselama, said last month it had rejected cooperation offers from both Aamulehti and Sanoma.
A number of suppliers have started to offer on-line economic news on the internet.
